rows.description: A child is told to sit properly, stay quiet and let guests eat first, and may resent missing a favourite dish. The child learns that home has a public face and a private one.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager is pulled from study to serve tea for unexpected relatives while a sibling is left alone. Honouring guests is real, but fairness in who serves, especially between daughters and sons, matters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A host smiles while wondering how long a relative will stay without warning. Indian norms make it hard to say no; gentle honest talk about timing protects both hospitality and the relationship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult brings a small gift, offers help in the kitchen, and leaves before the host is tired. Being a good guest is as much a skill as being a good host.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A host spends beyond means to impress visitors so as not to look poor. Generosity mixed with fear of judgement can become debt; warm simple welcome is still real hospitality.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young person sees that some cultures expect a host to insist and a guest to refuse twice, while others take a first no as final. Knowing the local rule avoids both offence and awkwardness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler grabs food, feeds others from their own hand and expects bites from everyone's plate. Sharing food is bonding in this stage, with no sense yet of clean or unclean.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child is told not to drink from another's glass or offer half-bitten food to deities, and starts sensing that some foods and touches are set apart. The child follows the rule before understanding it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child notices that a friend's home has different kitchen rules, such as no eggs or separate utensils. Curiosity is natural; asking kindly rather than mocking keeps friendships open.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager feels embarrassed by a smelly or unusual lunch, or proud of a home dish that friends beg to share. Food is identity, and how peers respond can teach either shame or pride.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame, embarrassment, pride
